cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken my key off the ring like you. Keep the spare or return it; let's settle what you meant by taking space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took mine off because it's bent. I meant one quiet evening, not moving out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, making room for the right key. Shall I get you a replacement?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. One that works. I want to be able to come home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the new key tonight. We'll call last week's space one evening, and leave it there.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies key removal as a space-related signal; B2 corrects damage and intended pause; A3 covers as replacement preparation; A5 makes B4 accepting access settle the old request as temporary.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 bent key supplies A3 replacement choice; B4 explicit wish to come home supplies A5 one-evening interpretation.

relationship.evidence: B4 directly states what it wants instead of asking A to explain a metaphor.

heightening.evidence: A5 lets B4 choice close the conflict by reinterpreting the earlier space request, a valid cooperative ending.

specificity.evidence: A1 keys/space and B2 bend make the physical mistake and emotional issue clear.
